questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: A classmate says Social Science is only a record of what happened long ago and of where things are located; correct this idea in about 45 words.

markingPoints.description: It is the systematic study of human society, and not only a record (1)
It also explains why events occur, how people live together and how environments influence life (1)
It covers how governments function, how economies operate and how the past and the present together shape the world (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Social Science is far more than a record. Along with telling us what happened and where things are located, it also explains why events occur, how people live together, how environments influence life, how governments function and how economies operate. It further shows how the past and the present together shape the world.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Compare what subjects like Physics, Chemistry and Biology study with what Social Science focuses on.

markingPoints.description: Physics, Chemistry and Biology study the natural world (1)
Social Science focuses on society, institutions, cultures and human interactions (1)
It explains why things happen and how different aspects of life are interconnected (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Subjects like Physics, Chemistry and Biology study the natural world. Social Science, by contrast, focuses on society, institutions, cultures and human interactions. It helps us understand not only what happens in our social world, but also why it happens and how different aspects of life are interconnected.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines
questions.stem: Rhea's history club wants to show that studying the past today is not the same as merely listening to stories; in steps, set out what History is, and how modern historians go about establishing timelines and understanding the past.

markingPoints.description: History is the study of human past, through which societies seek to understand people’s experiences, values and changes over time (1)
Different historical traditions have utilised different methods (1)
Some traditions emphasise moral and philosophical insight, while others offer documentary verification (1)
Modern historiography, by contrast, increasingly relies on empirical evidence (1)
It uses tools such as observation, human genetics, carbon-14 dating, archaeology and other scientific experimentation to establish timelines and understand the past (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: History is the study of human past, through which societies seek to understand people’s experiences, values, and changes over time. Step 2: Different historical traditions have utilised different methods. Step 3: Some traditions emphasise moral and philosophical insight, while others offer documentary verification. Step 4: Modern historiography, by contrast, increasingly relies on empirical evidence. Step 5: It uses tools such as observation, human genetics, carbon-14 dating, archaeology and other scientific experimentation, by which timelines are established and the past understood.

questions.stem:
Ananya's grandfather grows grain on a small plot where the river decides how much water reaches the crop. In the same village, a committee decides which festivals the village will keep, a trader buys the grain at the weekly market, and stories of an earlier harvest are retold every year. Ananya's grandmother says that nothing here can be understood on its own: the river, the committee, the market and the stories together have made the village what it is. Ananya decides to find out how these parts are joined.

(a) Name the four things that shape the lives of the people in Ananya's village. (b) State two things, other than what happened and where things are located, that the systematic study of human society explains. (c) Ananya's grandmother says that nothing in the village can be understood on its own; explain why the connections between these four things are the foundation of Social Science.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) The environment; the institutions that govern us; the economic activities that meet our needs; the traditions and ideas passed down through generations. (b) It explains why events occur and how people live together. (c) Human beings depend on each other, so these four forces shape lives together, and studying their intricate patterns and influences shows how different aspects of life are interconnected.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Kabir's class is doing a project on water. One group records how much of it reaches the fields and how the fields are laid out; another records who owns the wells, who repairs them, who decides how much water each household receives, and which older sayings about wells the village repeats. Kabir's classmates in another room are measuring the same water with instruments and writing down only what they measure. Their teacher asks both groups to say what each of them is studying, and Kabir notices that the two answers are not the same thing at all.

(a) Name three subjects that study the natural world. (b) State what Social Science focuses on instead. (c) Both groups study the same water; explain why studying it as part of human society gives an answer that measuring only the natural world cannot give.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Physics, Chemistry and Biology. (b) Social Science focuses on society, institutions, cultures and human interactions. (c) It also explains how environments influence life, how governments function and how economies operate, so it shows not only how much water there is but why people live as they do.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Meera's history club is preparing an exhibition on how people in her town live now. One member points out that the town's festivals, its market, the way its people arrange matters among themselves and the stories they tell about earlier times all belong together, so the club decides to look at the connections rather than at each item alone. A second member claims that Social Science should only tell the club what happened long ago. Meera disagrees and asks the club to write down what it is missing.

(a) Name four forces that shape the lives of human beings. (b) Apart from what happened and where things are located, state two things that Social Science explains. (c) The second member claims that Social Science should only record what happened long ago; explain what the past and the present together shape, and why that settles the argument.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) The environment; the institutions that govern us; the economic activities that meet our needs; the traditions and ideas passed down through generations. (b) It explains why events occur and how people live together. (c) The past and the present together shape the world, so Social Science explains how different aspects of life are interconnected, not merely what happened.
